doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bebop versus hard bop
summary: Jones sees little difference between the terms, possibly tempo or line smoothness.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Does the distinction between bebop and hard bop mean anything to you? Those are terms that are bandied about.
Well, bebop is a general term. Hardbop is almost the same thing. I don't think there's that much difference. When you hear one, you hear the other. I guess it just
depends on what tune you are playing. You can play a ballad, and be playing bebop. It may be hard to conceive, but it is possible.
Well, it’s that funky, earthy element. That seems to distinguish hard bop from bebop.

Maybe it is the tempos they make the distinction. Sometimes the line that is being played, if it is like a discombobulated, jerky line, maybe that is called hard bop. If it is a nice smooth even line, maybe that is bebop. I think it is a minor difference, if any. I may be wrong, but that is my take on it.
